items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: I had David Jones on tenor sax.

ctx.x: Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh.

kind of instruments? Well no, they had a regular band there. They had Joe Rubishu, Roy Evans, David Jones. What was that band? Tenor. He was playing tenor there. I forget who was playing piano at the time. Joe Rubishu was playing piano, but I mean I forget who was playing. Bass player? No, they didn't have bass player. Trumpet? There were four pieces there. Yeah, I'm trying to think now who was playing trumpet there. I don't know, Willie Pazio. I can't remember who was playing trumpet. Kaifer. Kaifer. Who is…

Let me get back to this end of time this time. When you first went there, that was the band they had there and they weren't using it after. No. And you went there and played a little. Did you join the band or just?
Who is at the La Vida with you? You were talking about that.

Oh, I mentioned the fellow that was at the La Vida with me already. Such as Lee Collins, uh, John Marrero, Simon Marrero, uh, Roy Evans was there with me on drums, and Alfred William on drums, and, uh, David Jones on tennis sax, Rubichaud on piano.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: David Jones played at the La Vida with me, too.

ctx.x: Now was that after, was that after Collins worked at the Astoria with Davy Jones? Or do you know?
And that was, um, oh, matter of fact, David Jones played at the La Vida with me, too.
Well, they were together at the, at the Astoria. Yeah.
